newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe to spin off Monterey Pacific unit.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe to spin off Monterey Pacific unit.

text.p: Santa Fe Energy Resources Inc., an independent oil and gas company, said Wednesday it will split into two companies to allow its businesses to operate more efficiently and improve access to capital markets.

Santa Fe said it filed for an initial public offering of about 7.9 million shares, or 17 percent of the common stock of its wholly owned subsidiary Monterey Resources Inc. Of this, 6.3 million will be offered in the United States and 1.6 million overseas.
Monterey Resources, based in Bakersfield, Calif., will assume mainly Santa Fe's oil-producing entities on the West Coast and $175 million in debt, a company spokesman said.
Santa Fe's western division holds reserves of about 214 milion barrels of oil and produces 46,000 barrels a day of oil and oil-equivalent natural gas from one of the nation's largest fields.
After the IPO, Santa Fe said it will spin off its remaining 85 percent stake in Monterey Resources to its shareholders late in the second quarter of 1997.

Santa Fe will keep oil and gas producing assets in West Texas and the Gulf of Mexico as well as promising international exploration and development projects, including those currently underway in Gabon and the Indonesian island of Sumatra.
Santa Fe said it also intends to buy back shares of its 7 percent series preferred stock at a later date. The conditions of the offer will be determined at that time.

R. Graham Whaling, senior vice president and chief financial officer of Santa Fe, has been named chairman and chief executive of Monterey Resources. David Kilpatrick, the manager of Santa Fe's western division, has been named president and chief operating officer.
James Payne will remain chairman and chief executive of Santa Fe.
Goldman, Sachs & Co. is the lead managing underwriter, and Morgan Stanley & Co. Inc. and Petrie Parkman & Co. are the co-managing underwriters in the United States.
Outside the United States, Goldman Sachs International is the lead managing underwriter, while Morgan Stanley & Co. International and Petrie Parkman & Co. are the co-managing underwriters.
Santa Fe's stock rose 75 cents to $13.75 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
